annotationRationale: Returning horses correspond exactly to divisors of the elapsed integer time from 1 through 10. Checking these divisor counts establishes the earliest qualifying time.
sourceMethod: Follows the official enumeration of divisor counts for times 1 through 12, clarifying why only integer times need checking and why only divisors through 10 count.

review.mathCheck: Positive return times are integer multiples of each horse's lap time. The divisor counts for times 1 through 11 are correctly listed and never exceed four. At 12, exactly 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 divide the time within the permitted range. Thus T=12 and its digit sum is 3, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA Solution 16 on page 5: enumerate restricted divisor counts through 12. The candidate also explicitly excludes noninteger return times.
review.annotationCheck: The method and rationale match the explanation. The supplied S=2520 does not require prime-factorization or divisor-count-formula annotations.
